In northeastern Afghanistan's isolated Wakhan Corridor, it was recorded by camera traps at 16 locations.  The snow leopard inhabits alpine and subalpine zones at elevations of 3,000 to 4,500 m (9,800 to 14,800 ft), but also lives at lower elevations in the northern part of its range.  In summer, it usually lives above the tree line on alpine meadows and in rocky regions at elevations of 2,700 to 6,000 m (8,900 to 19,700 ft).  In winter, it descends to elevations around 1,200 to 2,000 m (3,900 to 6,600 ft)
